newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Farm Council expected to agree veal crates ban.
newsitem.headline: Farm Council expected to agree veal crates ban.

text.p: Agreement is likely to be reached on phasing out veal crates and improving the diet of calves at next week's Farm Council, an Irish EU Presidency official said on Thursday.
"There are good prospects for reaching agreement," the official said.
In response to public indignation against confining calves in cramped crates, the Commission proposed on January 24 in COM(96)21 to change Directive 91/629 on minimum standards for protecting calves.
New and renovated veal crates would be banned from 1998 and all veal crates from 2008.

In March 1996, the Commission presented a supplementary proposal to improve calves' milky diet by providing fibre roughage and daily fresh drinking water while ensuring continued production of the pale meat prized by consumers.
Calves in crates would be inspected twice daily and should have enough room to lie down, rest, turn around and groom themselves without difficulty. They should not normally be tethered.
French and Italian farmers, the main users of veal crates, have protested that the proposal would ruin them.
The Commission has tried to take account of the social and economic impact of farmers with a 10-year phasing out period and some flexibility on the conditions.
